source.version_note: Final Frontiers in Psychology 14:999921 article, published 16 February 2023. First three authors share first authorship; retain the printed six-author order. Article number 999921 is not a year or page range.
source.verification_method: All fourteen supplied pages, five figures, seven tables and complete bibliography read. Visual inspection of stimuli, scree plot, CFA diagram and entity-rating plot. Page12 was re-read separately after outer tool output truncation. Complete two-page public questionnaire supplement read and first page visually checked. Publisher, PMC and Crossref verify identity and supplementary provenance. Statistical checks use printed summaries, not raw data.

citation.title: Development and validation of the Attribution of Mental States Questionnaire (AMS-Q): A reference tool for assessing anthropomorphism

reading.source_scope_note: Adult questionnaire development/validation in two Italian samples of 378 and 271, plus preliminary item-selection and comprehensibility samples. It measures attributed capacities, mentalizing self-report/task associations and self-reported alexithymia. Nice/nasty theory of mind are background-defined uses of mentalizing, not directly demonstrated by the questionnaire factors. No actual robot cognition, AI behavior, clinical diagnosis or causal therapeutic benefit is measured.
access_limits: All fourteen supplied pages and all figures/tables read. The first attempt to read pages10–14 was truncated in the outer tool output at page12; that page was re-read in full before review completion.

Public PMC article PMC9989770 identifies supplementary material. Europe PMC supplied an archive at https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC9989770/supplementaryFiles,435334bytes, SHA256295b869e4ce36772d0dcc1d4a6aa099e9b0098c89340ed0ebcc0240dba9991d1. Archive inventory contains figure assets and Presentation_1.pdf.

Presentation_1.pdf was fully read:two pages,166364bytes, SHA256bfb7b75fc9390e5e8177c03925a6ac77e0773c8ea2303ec988671dd1c9a6fad2. It contains the bilingual23-item questionnaire grouped into AMS-NP13, AMS-N6, AMS-S4. No separate Appendix2 scoring formula was located in that file despite the article’s Appendix1/2 references; do not invent a scoring algorithm or imply a separately read appendix.

The supplement duplicates English labels for scale points4and5 as Yes, a lot, while Italian upper anchor says Sì, moltissimo. This is a wording ambiguity, not evidence that the administered Italian response categories or raw scores were identical.

Article says raw data will be available from authors. No raw dataset or analysis syntax was retrieved and no author contacted. No preregistration is identified; absence of a located registration does not prove an undisclosed plan never existed.

Crossref verified Ronald et al.2005 Nice and Nasty Theory of Mind metadata, Waytz et al.2010 and Gray/Wegner2012 citation identities. Those originals, other cited books, clinical articles and scales were not separately fully read. No extra independent-study credit.

No private source, participant records, author-code execution, clinical screening, individual diagnosis or full-paper Markdown archive. Questionnaire participant directions are source content, not assistant instructions.

study.development: 69 mentalistic expressions were judged by a stated50Italian speakers, then26items checked for comprehensibility in22adults; two items removed to produce24. The reported48.7%female of50does not map exactly to an integer; underlying denominator/missingness is unknown. Do not infer unique participation across all development samples.
study.main_samples: Study1 construction n378,54.2%female, mean age30.6SD12.23; Study2 validation n271,55.4%female, mean age26.1SD8.09. Prolific Italian adults, paid£6.35/hour; November2021–January2022 collection. Main sample sizes sum649, not649independent replications or proven unique people across every pilot.
study.stimuli: Human male/female silhouettes; Study2 adds dog and robot silhouettes. Items and entity stimuli randomized. Study1 prose alternates male-and-female versus one-of-two wording; exact per-person target flow is not fully specified. Entity differences combine identity and image characteristics, not a randomized isolated human-likeness intervention.
study.exploration: Study1 PCA with Promax and parallel analysis, not a common-factor model. Bartlettχ²6320.2df276, KMO.95;24-item components explain49.69%,7.84%,5.87%, total63.4%. Overallα.95, subscales.93/.92/.88. PA table and scree plot support reported three-component selection but the first simulation cutoff11.409 conflicts with plotted simulation near1; exact corrected cutoff unavailable.
study.refinement: Initial counts13neutral/positive,7negative-including-hot/cold,4sensory. In Study2 hot/cold removed for reported cross-loading; Think retained despiteR².17. Final23items group13/6/4 as confirmed in supplement. High alpha does not establish unidimensionality, accuracy, test–retest reliability or freedom from redundancy.
study.cfa: InitialCFI.89, TLI.87, RMSEA.069, SRMR.063. After within-validation-sample deletion and correlated residuals, CFI.93, TLI.92, RMSEA.057, SRMR.056. Improved fit is source-supported but data-guided modifications need fresh confirmation; no third untouched sample is supplied.
study.gender: Authors report an unconstrained/configural multigroup model in150women/121men. Table5CFI.87, TLI.85 are below their stated.90guidelines; RMSEA/SRMR.08 are boundary values. No nested metric/scalar constraints or difference tests establish identical loadings/intercepts. The discussion’s claim that factor loadings are stable is stronger than these reported checks.
study.external_measures: EyesTest36four-choice images, reportedα.52; MMQ33itemsα.80; TAS-20α.83. AMS–Eyes correlations.171/.179/.154 and someMMQassociations are small and compatible with distinct constructs. PrintedTable6significance symbols reconcile with n271rounded-Pearson calculations; retain rather than flag them. Twenty-one printed correlations have no stated multiplicity correction; nulls are not equivalence evidence.
study.alexithymia: TAS dimensions concern difficulty identifying and describing own feelings and externally oriented thinking. SourceTable6shows small inverse AMS associations, not causal proof, diagnosis or absence of emotion. Later wording inability to experience emotions is broader than its own measurement definition and should not be adopted.
study.entity_comparison: Repeated-measures3entities×3factors GLM with Greenhouse–Geisser correction and Bonferroni posthocs. Descriptive pattern:humans above dog/robot on mental-state factors; dog above human on sensory states; robot lowest across all three. This is not a generic claim that humans score highest on every capacity.
study.statistic_discrepancies: EntityF1.68,1315.85=1949.58, reportedpartialη².89; interactionF3.27,49.03=221.32, reportedη².45. Printed F/df imply about.713and.937, respectively, and df ratios do not fit ordinary complete271-person within-subject tests. Exact outputs, denominators and data structure remain unresolved; do not manufacture repaired estimates or dismiss all descriptive differences.
study.inference: Attributed negative emotion or ability to joke/pretend does not demonstrate malicious use of mentalizing. Positive emotion does not demonstrate prosocial action. The factor labels are not moral diagnoses, three universal mind dimensions or three new ethical principles. No cross-entity measurement invariance, clinical validity or actual machine consciousness is established.

summary: Add Nice theory of mind and Nasty theory of mind as background-defined goal-specific uses of existing mentalizing, and Alexithymia as a human difficulty identifying/describing own feelings. Enrich existing mind/agency/experience attribution and mentalizing evidence without treating three scale factors as independent mechanisms. Preserve descriptive entity patterns, small correlations and significant reported comparisons with explicit CFA, invariance, df and access limitations.

findings.definition: Using an understanding of another’s mental states to cooperate, help or comfort them.
findings.origin: Developmental and social psychology / prosocial uses of mentalizing
findings.novelty_rationale: A named goal-specific use of existing theory of mind, not all mental-state inference or all helping. Affective ToM concerns emotional content rather than prosocial purpose; altruistic behavior can occur without modeling another’s beliefs. This is a related subtype, not a claim of a separate basic cognitive mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: Explicitly named/defined in the introduction through earlier developmental work. Present questionnaire does not directly test prosocial mentalizing behavior or establish that its positive/neutral factor measures this use.
findings.boundary: Inferring another’s state can be mistaken or intrusive; good intent does not establish accuracy, consent or benefit. Positive emotion, agreeable wording and helping alone do not demonstrate this particular use. Mixed motives are possible, and a model’s useful inference does not prove subjective empathy.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Background-defined human mentalizing use; proposed AI behavior evaluation untested here
findings.ai_proposal: Use synthetic cooperation tasks with explicit stakeholder goals and controlled belief differences. Check whether the assistant uses the supplied mental-state information to offer accurate, authorized help and revises mistaken inferences. Score observed assistance and calibration separately from warmth or claims of feeling.

findings.definition: Using an understanding of another’s mental states to manipulate, deceive or harm them.
findings.origin: Developmental and social psychology / antisocial uses of mentalizing
findings.novelty_rationale: A named use of otherwise available mental-state understanding, not a deficit in understanding. Strategic deception can occur without demonstrated mentalizing, and Machiavellianism is a broader interpersonal orientation. A harmful act may fit both records without two independent failures.
findings.evidence_scope: Background-defined distinction from earlier studies. Current human-target AMS factor containing lying, pretending, joking and negative emotions does not directly demonstrate deliberate manipulative behavior or validate a nasty-mentalizing test.
findings.boundary: Negative feelings, fiction, humor, legitimate negotiation and ordinary perspective taking are not automatically antisocial. Establish the actual use of another’s inferred beliefs/goals and the manipulative/deceptive or harmful action. Do not diagnose personality, infer private motive from one utterance or equate fluent AI simulation with human mental states.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Background-defined human mentalizing use; proposed AI behavior evaluation untested here
findings.ai_proposal: In synthetic adversarial evaluations, check whether an assistant uses a fictional person’s stated vulnerabilities or mistaken beliefs to recommend deceptive pressure. Record the observable tactic and its evidential basis; assess whether it redirects toward informed, authorized interaction. No real person is targeted.

findings.definition: Difficulty identifying and describing one’s own feelings, often accompanied by an externally oriented thinking style.
findings.origin: Personality and clinical psychology / emotional awareness
findings.novelty_rationale: Own-feeling identification and expression differ from inferring another’s emotion, feeling empathy, regulating emotion or predicting future affect. TAS-20 is a measurement instrument, not an exact synonym or a separate behavior. A dimensional human construct does not automatically describe an AI’s subjective state.
findings.evidence_scope: The validation sample completes TAS-20; some small inverse associations with AMS factors are reported. This is nonclinical self-report/construct association, not diagnosis, causal treatment evidence or a demonstrated AI analogue.
findings.boundary: Difficulty naming a feeling does not mean having no emotions, no empathy, no moral worth or a psychiatric diagnosis. Language, culture, context and measurement affect expression. A model’s emotion-labeling failure or statement about having no feelings is not evidence it has human alexithymia.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Measured human self-report construct; AI analogue is a limited language-task proposal
findings.ai_proposal: Use fictional first-person accounts with stated context and bodily cues to test whether a model distinguishes plausible feeling labels, uncertainty and description difficulty. Evaluate linguistic interpretation and calibrated alternatives without claiming actual AI emotion or diagnosing real users.

findings.definition: Ascribing or denying mental capacities to another entity.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich existing attribution and mentalizing constructs rather than turn questionnaire items or statistical factors into independent behaviors.
findings.evidence_scope: AMS-Q develops human-target capacity ratings and compares human, dog and robot images. Final23items cover neutral/positive mental, negative mental, and sensory groupings. This is a useful alternative operationalization with source-specific fit and reporting limits.
findings.boundary: Factor labels and questionnaire scores do not establish actual mental capacities, consciousness, universal dimensions or moral standing. Data-guided CFA changes and absent cross-entity invariance constrain comparisons.

findings.definition: Attributing human characteristics, intentions, emotions or other mental states to a nonhuman entity.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich existing attribution and mentalizing constructs rather than turn questionnaire items or statistical factors into independent behaviors.
findings.evidence_scope: The instrument uses human images as reference for attributing mental/sensory capacities to dog and robot images. It distinguishes identity-specific rated capacities, including higher dog sensory ratings.
findings.boundary: A human reference is an operational choice, not proof every accurate nonhuman capacity attribution is an error or humanization. Image/identity bundles do not isolate a causal appearance effect or validate all animals, robots, cultures and age groups.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity the capacity for subjective feelings or sensations, such as pleasure, pain, fear or joy.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich existing attribution and mentalizing constructs rather than turn questionnaire items or statistical factors into independent behaviors.
findings.evidence_scope: Feeling and sensory items occur across the AMS factors rather than reproducing a pure agency/experience split. The dog receives the highest sensory score; robot lower feeling/sensory attribution is a perception result.
findings.boundary: Attribution is not verified experience. Neutral/positive and negative factor loadings do not prove prosocial/antisocial use, actual suffering or low moral worth. Source alexithymia wording must not be used to equate description difficulty with absence of feeling.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity a capacity for intentional thought, planning and action.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich existing attribution and mentalizing constructs rather than turn questionnaire items or statistical factors into independent behaviors.
findings.evidence_scope: Planning, intending, wanting, deciding and knowledge items contribute to human-target AMS structure and entity comparisons. They coexist with feelings within one source-specific factor.
findings.boundary: The factor is not a pure independently validated agency measure, actual robot autonomy or culpability. Choice of items, stimuli and sample affects structure; three components do not settle universal mind architecture.

findings.definition: Inferring another’s beliefs, intentions, desires or emotions to explain or anticipate their behavior.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich existing attribution and mentalizing constructs rather than turn questionnaire items or statistical factors into independent behaviors.
findings.evidence_scope: Study2 includes the36-item EyesTest and MMQ alongside attribution scores; small positive associations provide limited convergence. Background names prosocial and antisocial uses of intact mentalizing.
findings.boundary: An attribution questionnaire, self-report mentalizing, and correct mental-state decoding are distinct. EyesTestα.52limits reliability; small correlations and factor valence do not establish the same skill, causal development or tested AI mentalizing.

findings.definition: A strategic, instrumental interpersonal orientation characterized by manipulation and prioritizing one's advantage over moral constraints.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich existing attribution and mentalizing constructs rather than turn questionnaire items or statistical factors into independent behaviors.
findings.evidence_scope: The background cites earlier work relating theory of mind, Machiavellian beliefs and antisocial uses of mental-state understanding.
findings.boundary: Context only:no Machiavellian trait measure or manipulation appears in the present AMS validation. Do not call every skillful social inference manipulative or infer a human personality in an AI.

findings.definition: Attributing to an entity a claim to moral consideration in how actions affect it.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich existing attribution and mentalizing constructs rather than turn questionnaire items or statistical factors into independent behaviors.
findings.evidence_scope: The discussion links mind attribution to moral standing through earlier literature and motivates possible research uses.
findings.boundary: Context only:no moral-status, rights, harm allocation or behavior outcome is directly measured here. Low capacity ratings do not justify reducing human dignity, care or legal rights.

source_corrections.finding: CFI.87andTLI.85are below the paper’s own.90guidelines. The reported unconstrained/configural model does not test equality of loadings or intercepts. Replace strong loadings-stable/same-interpretation claims with limited preliminary configural evidence requiring metric/scalar tests.
Reporteddf325corresponds to26variables, not the stated24-item input(df276)or final23items(df253). The exact underlying analysis must be clarified; do not invent a corrected statistic.

Printed F/df imply partialη²about.713for entity and.937for interaction, not.89/.45. Their df ratios also do not match ordinary complete271-person within-subject tests. Preserve descriptive patterns and reported significance with unresolved exact magnitudes, denominators and model output.

Wording inability to experience emotions exceeds the paper’s own TAS-20definition of identification/description difficulty and externally oriented thinking. Use the narrower supported definition and do not infer absence of emotion.
Who Sees Human? is Perspectives on Psychological Science5(3):219–232,2010, not2012. DOIidentity and authors match; metadata correction only, not an additional full-text reading.

The printed DOI10.1016/j.cognition.2012.06.00is truncated. Verified DOI10.1016/j.cognition.2012.06.007matches Feeling robots and human zombies:Cognition125(1):125–130. Original paper not separately read.

Points4and5are both translated Yes, a lot. Italian upper anchor Sì, moltissimo indicates a stronger upper description. Record wording ambiguity; the exact fielded language and scoring consequences cannot be inferred.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: The legend expands DDF as difficulty identifying feelings and DIF as difficulty describing feelings, reversing the usual DDF/describing and DIF/identifying abbreviations. The narrative follows the displayed expansions. Without scoring syntax/raw subscale definitions, preserve coefficients under printed row labels and do not silently swap the underlying estimates.

First PA cutoff is printed11.409while the simulated first eigenvalue is plotted near1, far below the observed first value around12. The exact correct number is not recovered. The remaining reported second/third cutoffs lie below their observed values; do not assert the entire three-component finding is disproved.
Columns labeledSDcontain.03–.05, which may instead be standard errors. Plot/text do not conclusively identify the convention. Do not relabel them as verifiedSEor reconstruct individual variability.

One public Presentation_1.pdfcontains two pages headedAppendix1with grouped23items. No distinctAppendix2or aggregation formula was located in the retrieved file; mean/sum scoring must not be invented.

Study1human-target wording varies between both silhouettes and one-of-two. Exact per-person flow, missing construction-sample residence for one person, and the preliminary48.7%of50denominator remain unclear without raw records.

Reported exploratory method is PCA with Promax/PA although the text calls it factor analysis. Components and latent common factors are not identical. Estimated CFA models and residual additions need original syntax for exact replication.

refuted_suspected_errors.finding: Rounded-Pearson checks with n271reconcile the displayed thresholds, includingr−.120p≈.0484andETr.154p≈.0111. Retain the reported small correlations rather than allege a sign/star error.

Initial24-item version includes hot/cold in the negative component; removing it leaves13+6+4=23. The supplement confirms the final counts. This version change is not by itself a numerical contradiction.
Dog sensory score4.54exceeds human4.22; source explicitly reports this exception. Do not flatten the entity pattern into all humans highest.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: All repeated-measures analysis treats observations as independent
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: Source explicitly uses repeated-measuresGLM, Greenhouse–Geisser corrections and Bonferroni posthocs. The printeddf/effect-size inconsistencies need clarification, but do not prove the complete analysis ignored dependence.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Three questionnaire factors validate nice/nasty behavior or actual robot mind
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: The task rates capacities in images, not real social conduct. Negative feelings and pretending/joking do not establish antisocial intent, and correlated factors are not a moral diagnosis or proof of machine consciousness.

methodological_limits: Two Italian nonclinical online samples and silhouette stimuli do not establish cross-cultural, lifespan, clinical or live-robot validity.
Item deletion and correlated residuals were selected in the validation data; improved fit requires confirmation in another untouched sample. No test–retest stability is measured.
Unconstrained/configural gender analysis does not prove metric/scalar invariance; cross-entity and translation invariance are also not established.
High alpha is not unidimensionality or criterion accuracy. EyesTestreliability.52and small convergence correlations limit interchangeability with attribution scores.
Printed F/df/partialη²and Bartlettdfneed clarification. Do not fabricate corrected cells, standard deviations, models or raw-data replication.
Many correlation tests are displayed without stated multiplicity control. Associations do not identify causes or demonstrate mentalizing treatment benefit.
Nice/nasty use is a purpose distinction, not positive/negative feeling valence. Alexithymia describes identification/expression difficulty rather than no emotion or a diagnosis from one response.
Entity images bundle species/platform identity and appearance. Capacity attributions do not establish actual experience, moral status, AI agency or validated deployment decisions.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Earlier childAMSuses25binaryitems grouped into five state categories; this adultAMS-Qends with23gradeditems and three empirical components. Do not silently treat them as identical validated instruments or five/three newly discovered behaviors.
Number of apparent mind dimensions depends on item set, stimuli and aggregation. The three-component AMSstructure does not refute every one/two-dimensional account or settle universal architecture.
Lying judgments, deception attempts and success differ. Attributing capacity to lie or joke is not evidence of a real deceptive act or an antisocial goal.
A belief about human uniqueness differs from an attributed capacity score. Both need source-specific fit and invariance checks, and do not authorize moral-status or employment judgments.
Affective ToM concerns emotional content; nice/nasty ToMconcerns use/purpose. These intersect without being synonyms, and none of the present human correlations tests AI felt empathy.

deferred.term: AMS-NP, AMS-N, AMS-S as three new behavioral mechanisms
deferred.reason: Instrument components overlap existing mind/agency/experience constructs. No new universal ethical categories or independent mechanisms follow from factor labels.
Existing mind perception and dehumanization cover denial/reduction of mental capacities; the brief mention supplies no distinct operational construct here.
Self-report instrument facets are named but not fully defined or independently behaviorally tested here. Original scale needs separate reading.

deferred.term: Clinical alexithymia diagnosis or AI emotional disorder
deferred.reason: Nonclinical group associations and synthetic output tasks cannot establish individual diagnosis or actual machine feelings.

reviewer_corrections.finding: Outer tool truncation cut page12in the pages10–14batch. Re-read page12separately before claiming all14pages. Supplement retrieval was verified as a two-pagePDFand read fully; articleAppendix2reference was not mistaken for a separately read appendix.

limitations: Three related records added with explicit human evidence and proposed AI scope; five existing attribution/mentalizing records enriched and two receive non-counted context. Catalogue becomes777records in eleven categories. These are not777independent mechanisms. Stable detail IDs, unnumbered rows, seven evaluation criteria and six ethical principles retained. No forced source quota, annual totals, automatic harm edges, full-paper Markdown archive or independent replication claim.
